questions.q: What is democracy? Describe its essential features.
answer: Democracy is a form of government in which the rulers are elected by the people, famously described by Abraham Lincoln as government of the people, by the people and for the people.

answer.text: The final decision-making power must rest with those chosen by the people, not with unelected persons.
Elections must be held regularly, offer a real choice, and allow the ruling party to be voted out of power.
Each adult must have one vote, and each vote must have equal value — one person, one vote, one value.
The elected government must rule within the limits set by the Constitution and the law, and must respect the fundamental rights of citizens.

questions.q: Give arguments for and against democracy, and explain why it is considered the best form of government.

answer.text: Democracy is more accountable and responsive to the people, since rulers must answer to voters. It improves the quality of decisions through discussion and consultation, provides a peaceful way to resolve conflicts, and enhances the dignity of citizens by treating them as equals.
Critics point out that democracy can be unstable and slow, is marked by constant political competition, and can involve corruption and poor leadership.

Despite these weaknesses, democracy is better than the alternatives because it is the only form of government that allows citizens to correct its own mistakes, peacefully change their rulers, and hold power to account.
